name: Selection weights: rare mornings count more, capped, asked plain
non_visual_rationale: Selection weights exist to unbias a stored number; nothing here has pixels. No template, string, style or route is touched, and no call log exists at launch, so every morning weighs the same and the published surface is byte-identical. U1-U8 and a Vera walk are N/A.
criteria_delivered: 1. w_select = min(3, P_bar / P_hat(decile)), by published-score decile read from log/calls/v1/, over the trailing ninety days, pooled across spots and blind to which spot a morning belongs to. The window is load-bearing rather than decorative: shortening it to ten days fails both acceptance examples (mutation R4).

2. An extra morning on a rarely-reported kind of day moves the stored difference further than the same morning on an often-reported kind. On the fixture, a kind of morning reported four times in twenty against one reported sixteen times in twenty.

3. A push_solicited morning gets w_select = 1 exactly. Proven as equality against a morning the site published no call for at all, which carries no rarity bonus by construction -- and separately as an inequality against the same morning volunteered, so the trigger is provably read rather than provably ignored.

4. The cap of three is a unit law over generated histories, with a never-reported decile drawn deliberately alongside whatever the generator produced. Without the cap that decile's weight is Infinity, which is not a number a stored correction file can carry.
scope_note: The accepted roadmap names weights.ts, inputs.ts and the unit laws. Three more were touched and had to be. constants.ts: the cap and the window are declared numbers with one home. residuals.ts: the sample now carries whether the site ASKED for that morning, which is the one thing 06 section 6.3 exempts. fit.ts: the propensity table needs the run's own clock for the trailing window and the whole raw log for the numerator, and neither may be reached for from inside a pure function, so it is built at the boundary and handed inward -- the same shape the trust gate and the seed roster already use.
design_decisions_not_stated_upstream: A MORNING NOBODY PUBLISHED A CALL FOR CARRIES NO SELECTION WEIGHT AT ALL, and is left at 1. 06 section 6.3 buckets days by 'the published score decile that was live that morning' and says nothing about a morning with no published call. There is no propensity to invert there: the site never told anybody what to expect, so the report cannot have been selected on a published score. Inventing a decile for it would be inventing the very quantity the weight is supposed to measure. This default is also what makes criterion 3 provable by equality rather than by arithmetic.

THE NUMERATOR IS BUILT FROM THE RAW OBSERVATION LOG, NOT THE TRUST-ELIGIBLE ONE. Every other count in this lane is post-eligibility, deliberately (06 section 7). This one is not, and the reason is what is being modelled: P(report | conditions) is a human behaviour -- people post when it looks good -- and a morning somebody reported WAS reported whether or not the fit was later willing to weigh their sample. Filtering it would make the measured reporting rate a property of the trust gate rather than of the community. No stored number differs today, since the trust gate ships as a proven no-op.

A MORNING WITH MORE THAN ONE PUBLISHED CALL IS BUCKETED BY THE LAST ONE IN KEY ORDER. The log carries one object per build per region, so a day can hold several. The last in key order is the most recent build before that morning, which is what 06 section 6.3's phrase 'was live that morning' names. Stated because the log's shape makes it a real choice and the answer changes which decile a morning lands in.

A DECILE NOBODY EVER REPORTED IS PAID THE CAP, not an infinity and not a zero. min(3, P_bar / 0) is the cap by arithmetic, but only if the division is allowed to happen; the code says so directly instead, because an Infinity intermediate that happens to be clipped is a NaN waiting for the next change. The unit property draws that decile deliberately rather than hoping a free generator finds it -- 03-04's lesson.

SELECTION IS APPLIED AT THE SAME POINT AS CONCORDANCE, after the sample list is final. 06 section 6 says the weights are multiplicative, so their order among themselves cannot matter; what matters is that both come after the two ROBUST stages, which change the list rather than the weights. Concordance measures values and not weights, so the two are genuinely independent.
acceptance: tests/acceptance/f-forecast-learns-from-the-beach/a-rarely-reported-morning-counts-for-more.test.ts, two examples over the real runLearningFitOnce port with a call log in the same in-memory store. Twenty quiet mornings published in the second decile of which four were reported, twenty good mornings published in the eighth of which sixteen were reported, and one morning nobody published a call for. THE FIXTURE ISOLATES SELECTION FROM EVERY OTHER WEIGHT, which is what makes the comparison honest: the extra morning each run adds agrees EXACTLY with the report already standing on that day, so no reporter disagrees with anybody and concordance is a flat 1 everywhere; and it always lands on a day that already carried a report, so the propensity table it is weighed against is identical in every run. The only thing that differs between runs is w_select. The days also run backwards from the run's own clock, so all of them sit inside the trailing ninety and the window is exercised rather than sidestepped.
unit_law: Two fast-check properties in tests/unit/learning-weight-laws.test.ts against selectionWeightByMorning, whose exported signature is its port. (1) THE CAP, over generated histories of up to eight deciles with a never-reported decile drawn deliberately alongside them: every weight is finite, at most three, and strictly above zero. (2) MONOTONICITY: a kind of morning reported less often is never paid less than one reported more often -- the property that says the propensity is inverted rather than merely applied, and the one mutation R2 falls to.
test_budget: Behaviours: (1) a rarely-reported kind of morning counts for more, (2) an asked-for morning carries no rarity bonus, (3) the cap. Three behaviours, budget 6. Delivered 4: 2 acceptance examples and 2 unit properties.
red_evidence: The acceptance file was written first and run against the 04-03 body. Both examples RED with semantic AssertionErrors: 'one more report on a kind of morning reported four times in twenty moved the stored difference 0.06519480519480518, no further than the 0.06519480519480518 the same report moves it on a kind reported sixteen times in twenty' -- the two movements identical to the last digit, which is exactly what no selection weighting looks like -- and 'the same quiet morning stored 0.13090909090909086 whether the site asked for it or somebody volunteered it: the trigger is not being read at all'. The two unit properties were run against the absent function, then each was falsified by its own targeted mutation below.
falsifiability_evidence: Four controlled mutations, each planted alone against a byte-snapshot of src/learning, each reverted, the revert verified with diff -r ('REVERT CLEAN'), the suite re-run green. (R1) the cap removed: caught by the cap property, 'playa-venao 2026-01-02 was weighed at Infinity, which is not a number a stored correction file can carry'. (R2) the propensity applied the right way up instead of inverted -- common mornings paid MORE: caught twice, by the monotonicity property and by the acceptance example, where the quiet morning's movement collapses to 0.021 against the popular morning's 0.081. (R3) the solicited exemption dropped, so an asked-for morning is paid the rarity bonus like any other: caught by the acceptance guard. (R4) the trailing window shortened from ninety days to ten: caught by BOTH acceptance examples, which is what makes the window load-bearing rather than a number in a comment.
